title: United Express 2415
summary: United Express Flight 2415 crashed 400 feet short of runway 21R at Tri-Cities Airport on December 26, 1989, during final approach. The aircraft had accumulated airframe icing after the captain declined de-icing at Yakima, and slowed to 110 knots while descending steeply. The combination of icing, low speed, and excessive descent rate resulted in loss of control.
probable_cause: The National Transportation Safety Board determined that the combination of airframe icing, failure to obtain ground de-icing, low airspeed, and excessive descent rate resulted in loss of control of the aircraft during approach.

factors.evidence: Captain Roberts declined de-icing at Yakima despite offers
Ice had likely built up on the plane's wings during the flight in light to moderate mixed icing
Flight 2415 had slowed to 110 knots as it attempted to descend
The combination of an excessively steep descent, low speed, and aircraft icing likely resulted in loss of control

events.text: Captain Roberts declined de-icing at Yakima despite offers
Flight 2415 departed Yakima en route to Pasco and climbed to a cruising altitude of 11000 ft
Flight 2415 was cleared for an Instrument Landing System approach to runway 21R
Flight 2415 observed flying higher than normal for final approach and descending faster than normal
Aircraft struck the ground 400 ft short of runway 21R
